summary: Chinese has two words for 'or'. 还是 asks the listener to pick one (which one?), so it lives in questions and in 'whether A or B' clauses. 或者 simply lists possibilities in a statement (either is fine). Ask yourself: is the choice still open and being asked about? Then 还是. 还是 also means 'still' and, with 吧, 'had better'.

subs.label: 还是 in a choice question
subs.focus: A direct question that offers two options and expects the listener to pick one. The learner must choose 还是, not 或者. Classic mistake: 你喝茶或者咖啡? Make the sentence clearly a question that wants a pick (question mark, 你 subject, no 吗), and repeat or drop the verb naturally (你坐地铁还是打车?).

subs.label: No 吗 with 还是
subs.focus: A 还是 question is already a question, so 吗 cannot be added. The learner must decide to leave the end of the sentence empty (∅) or use 呢, never 吗. Classic mistake: 你喝茶还是咖啡吗? Use cloze with ∅ / 吗, judge items, and rewrites from a 吗 question into a choice question.

subs.label: 还是 for 'whether A or B'
subs.focus: A statement that contains an unanswered choice after 不知道, 不确定, 没想好, 还没决定, 问, 想知道, 告诉我, 猜. The whole sentence ends in a full stop but the inner clause is still a question, so it takes 还是. Classic mistake: using 或者 because the sentence is not a question (我不知道他去或者不去). Include A-or-not-A shapes (去还是不去).

subs.label: 或者 in statements
subs.focus: A statement, suggestion or instruction listing alternatives without asking anyone to pick: must be 或者, not 还是. Classic mistake: 我周末看书还是看电影 as a statement. Keep items free of 无论/不管 and of 不知道-type verbs so only 或者 fits; good frames: 可以, 都行, 常常, 想/打算.

subs.label: 还是…吧: had better
subs.focus: 还是 + verb phrase (+ 吧) as mild advice or a preference after weighing options: 'had better'. Learner must pick 还是 (not 或者/还有) and place it after the subject, before the verb. Classic mistake: 还是 at the end, or reading it as 'or'. Add a reason clause (rain, traffic, price) to force the reading.

subs.label: 还是 = still
subs.focus: 还是 as the adverb 'still, all the same': unchanged situation or same result despite something. Learner must place it after the subject, before the verb or adjective, and not choose 或者/也是. Frames: 虽然…还是…, 说了很多次他还是… Classic mistake: 还是 before the subject or after the verb.

subs.label: 无论/不管 A 还是 B, 都…
subs.focus: After 无论/不管, options join with 还是 and the main clause needs 都. Classic mistakes: dropping 都, putting 都 before the subject, joining with 和. Never test 还是 against 或者 here (或者 is also heard after 无论/不管); test 都, its position, or 还是 against 和/也/吗.

rules.rule: When you ask someone to pick between options, join the options with 还是.
rules.pattern: Subject + Verb + A + 还是 + (Verb) + B + ?

examples.zh: 你喝茶还是喝咖啡？
examples.py: nǐ hē chá hái shì hē kā fēi
examples.en: Will you have tea or coffee?

examples.zh: 我们今天去还是明天去？
examples.py: wǒ men jīn tiān qù hái shì míng tiān qù
examples.en: Are we going today or tomorrow?

examples.zh: 这是你的手机还是他的手机？
examples.py: zhè shì nǐ de shǒu jī hái shì tā de shǒu jī
examples.en: Is this your phone or his?

rules.note: The verb is often repeated before the second option (喝茶还是喝咖啡), and it can be left out when the options are simple nouns (喝茶还是咖啡). When the verb is 是, it is not said twice: 是你的还是他的, not 还是是他的.

rules.rule: A choice can be between whole clauses with different subjects: 还是 goes before the second clause.
rules.pattern: A clause + 还是 + B clause + ?

examples.zh: 你来我家还是我去你家？
examples.py: nǐ lái wǒ jiā hái shì wǒ qù nǐ jiā
examples.en: Will you come to my place or shall I go to yours?

examples.zh: 你做饭还是我做饭？
examples.py: nǐ zuò fàn hái shì wǒ zuò fàn
examples.en: Are you cooking or am I?

rules.rule: Never end a 还是 choice question with 吗. Leave the end bare, or add 呢 to soften it.

examples.zh: 你坐地铁还是打车？
examples.py: nǐ zuò dì tiě hái shì dǎ chē
examples.en: Are you taking the subway or a taxi?

examples.zh: 我们在家吃还是出去吃呢？
examples.py: wǒ men zài jiā chī hái shì chū qù chī ne
examples.en: Shall we eat at home or eat out?

rules.note: 吗 turns a statement into a yes/no question; a 还是 question cannot be answered yes or no. A yes/no question that merely mentions alternatives uses 或者 and can take 吗: 你周六或者周日有空吗? (Are you free on Saturday or Sunday? Answer: yes/no.)

rules.rule: Inside a statement, an undecided or unknown choice ('whether A or B') still takes 还是.
rules.pattern: 不知道 / 没想好 / 问 / 想知道 + A + 还是 + B

examples.zh: 我不知道他去还是不去。
examples.py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā qù hái shì bù qù
examples.en: I don't know whether he is going or not.

examples.zh: 我还没想好买红的还是买蓝的。
examples.py: wǒ hái méi xiǎng hǎo mǎi hóng de hái shì mǎi lán de
examples.en: I haven't decided whether to buy the red one or the blue one.

examples.zh: 请告诉我你要大的还是小的。
examples.py: qǐng gào su wǒ nǐ yào dà de hái shì xiǎo de
examples.en: Please tell me whether you want the big one or the small one.

rules.note: The test is not the punctuation but whether the choice is still open. No 吗 here either.

rules.rule: In a statement that just lists alternatives (either is possible or fine), use 或者.
rules.pattern: A + 或者 + B + (都) + Verb / comment

examples.zh: 周六或者周日都行。
examples.py: zhōu liù huò zhě zhōu rì dōu xíng
examples.en: Saturday or Sunday is fine.

examples.zh: 我周末常常看书或者看电影。
examples.py: wǒ zhōu mò cháng cháng kàn shū huò zhě kàn diàn yǐng
examples.en: On weekends I often read or watch a film.

examples.zh: 你可以给我打电话或者发短信。
examples.py: nǐ kě yǐ gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà huò zhě fā duǎn xìn
examples.en: You can call me or send me a text.

rules.note: 或者 can be shortened to 或 in writing. In negative statements Chinese usually avoids 'or' altogether: 我不喝茶,也不喝咖啡 (I don't drink tea or coffee).

rules.rule: 还是 + verb phrase + 吧 gives the option you settle on after thinking it over: 'had better', 'let's … instead'.

examples.zh: 外面下雨了，我们还是坐地铁吧。
examples.py: wài miàn xià yǔ le wǒ men hái shì zuò dì tiě ba
examples.en: It's raining outside; we'd better take the subway.

examples.zh: 太晚了，你还是明天再去吧。
examples.py: tài wǎn le nǐ hái shì míng tiān zài qù ba
examples.en: It's too late; you'd better go tomorrow.

examples.zh: 我觉得还是这件好看。
examples.py: wǒ jué de hái shì zhè jiàn hǎo kàn
examples.en: I think this one looks better after all.

rules.note: 还是 goes after the subject and before the verb, or before the preferred thing when a comment follows (还是这件好看). 吧 is usual in suggestions but not required when you state your own preference.

rules.rule: 还是 before a verb or adjective means 'still': nothing has changed, or the result is the same in spite of something.

examples.zh: 我说了三遍，他还是不明白。
examples.py: wǒ shuō le sān biàn tā hái shì bù míng bai
examples.en: I said it three times and he still doesn't understand.

examples.zh: 虽然很累，她还是去上班了。
examples.py: suī rán hěn lèi tā hái shì qù shàng bān le
examples.en: Although she was tired, she still went to work.

examples.zh: 这么多年了，你还是这么年轻。
examples.py: zhè me duō nián le nǐ hái shì zhè me nián qīng
examples.en: After all these years you're still so young.

rules.note: 还是 follows the subject: 他还是不明白, not 还是他不明白. For an action simply continuing, 还 alone is more common (他还在睡觉); 还是 stresses 'same as before' or 'even so'.

rules.rule: After 无论 or 不管, join the options with 还是 and put 都 before the main verb: 'whether A or B, …'.
rules.pattern: 无论 / 不管 + A + 还是 + B + Subject + 都 + Verb

examples.zh: 不管刮风还是下雨，他都去跑步。
examples.py: bù guǎn guā fēng hái shì xià yǔ tā dōu qù pǎo bù
examples.en: Whether it's windy or rainy, he goes running.

examples.zh: 无论大人还是孩子都喜欢这个地方。
examples.py: wú lùn dà rén hái shì hái zi dōu xǐ huan zhè ge dì fang
examples.en: Both adults and children like this place.

examples.zh: 不管你来还是不来，都告诉我一声。
examples.py: bù guǎn nǐ lái hái shì bù lái dōu gào su wǒ yī shēng
examples.en: Whether you come or not, let me know.

rules.note: 都 comes after the subject of the main clause, never before it. 还是 is the standard join here, but 或者 is also heard after 无论/不管, so do not treat 或者 as an error in this frame; the fixed points are 无论/不管 and 都.

right.py: nǐ hē chá hái shì kā fēi
right.en: Will you have tea or coffee?

contrasts.why: You are asking the listener to pick one, so the 'or' must be 还是. 或者 only lists possibilities and cannot ask 'which one?'.

contrasts.wrong: 你想吃米饭还是面条吗？

right.py: nǐ xiǎng chī mǐ fàn hái shì miàn tiáo
right.en: Do you want rice or noodles?

contrasts.why: 还是 already makes the sentence a question. 吗 asks for yes or no, which cannot answer 'rice or noodles'.

contrasts.wrong: 我下午去打球还是游泳。

right.zh: 我下午去打球或者游泳。
right.py: wǒ xià wǔ qù dǎ qiú huò zhě yóu yǒng
right.en: This afternoon I'll go play ball or swim.

contrasts.why: This is a plain statement of two possible plans; nobody is being asked to choose. Statements use 或者.

contrasts.wrong: 我不知道她是老师或者学生。

right.zh: 我不知道她是老师还是学生。
right.py: wǒ bù zhī dào tā shì lǎo shī hái shì xué sheng
right.en: I don't know whether she is a teacher or a student.

contrasts.why: After 不知道 the choice is still an open question, even though the sentence ends with a full stop. An open choice takes 还是.

contrasts.wrong: 路上车太多，我们坐地铁还是吧。

right.zh: 路上车太多，我们还是坐地铁吧。
right.py: lù shang chē tài duō wǒ men hái shì zuò dì tiě ba
right.en: There's too much traffic; we'd better take the subway.

contrasts.why: 还是 meaning 'had better' is an adverb: it goes after the subject and before the verb, not at the end next to 吧.

contrasts.wrong: 我说了很多次，还是他不听。

right.zh: 我说了很多次，他还是不听。
right.py: wǒ shuō le hěn duō cì tā hái shì bù tīng
right.en: I've said it many times, but he still doesn't listen.

contrasts.why: 还是 meaning 'still' is an adverb and follows the subject of its clause (他), directly before 不听.

right.zh: 不管贵还是便宜，我都买。
right.py: bù guǎn guì hái shì pián yi wǒ dōu mǎi
right.en: Whether it's expensive or cheap, I'll buy it.

contrasts.why: 不管/无论 needs 都 (or 也) in the main clause to say 'in every case'. English has no word there, so learners drop it.

contrasts.wrong: 不管晴天还是雨天，都他骑车上班。

right.zh: 不管晴天还是雨天，他都骑车上班。
right.py: bù guǎn qíng tiān hái shì yǔ tiān tā dōu qí chē shàng bān
right.en: Rain or shine, he cycles to work.

contrasts.why: 都 is an adverb: it comes after the subject 他 and before the verb phrase, never in front of the subject.

cheat: Asking someone to pick one? 还是. Just listing what's possible? 或者.
还是 question: no 吗. Bare ending or 呢.
After 不知道, 没想好, 问, 想知道, 告诉我: the choice is still open, so 还是 even with a full stop.
Can the answer be yes or no (…有空吗?)? Then the 'or' inside it is 或者.
还是 + verb + 吧 with no second option = 'had better'. Subject first, then 还是.
还是 right before a verb or adjective, after 虽然 or 'many times' = 'still'.
无论 / 不管 A 还是 B: don't forget 都 after the subject.
